\documentclass[11pt]{article}\usepackage[margin=1in]{geometry}\usepackage{amsmath,amsthm}\newtheorem{theorem}{Theorem}\newtheorem{remark}{Remark}
\title{An Integer Topology Carrier Beyond Center Flux}\author{}\date{21 July 2026}\begin{document}\maketitle
\begin{abstract}We prove that the six mod-two center labels cannot retain integer four-dimensional flux pairing and define the minimal additional integer carrier in the abelian embedded calibration.\end{abstract}
For integral fluxes $(n_{01},n_{02},n_{03},n_{12},n_{13},n_{23})$, define
\[Q_{\rm Pf}=n_{01}n_{23}-n_{02}n_{13}+n_{03}n_{12}.\]
\begin{theorem}Reduction of the six fluxes modulo two does not determine $Q_{\rm Pf}$. Indeed, the family
\[(2k,0,0,0,0,2k)\]
has fixed zero center label and charge $4k^2$. Hence integer charge is unbounded on one center-label fiber. Moreover $Q_{\rm Pf}^2$ is the determinant of the associated antisymmetric flux matrix.\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}Direct substitution gives zero mod-two flux and charge $4k^2$. The determinant identity is the standard four-dimensional Pfaffian formula and also follows by expansion of the displayed antisymmetric matrix.\end{proof}
The retained topology state must therefore include an integer lift in addition to the center label.
\begin{remark}This is an exact integral-flux and embedded-abelian calibration. It is not a construction of the full nonabelian lattice second Chern class, nor a sector-weight estimate.\end{remark}\end{document}
